situation: My brother and sister aren't speaking because of a fight over who hosts Christmas with our dad. Both keep calling me to vent. I want to help without being in the middle. My sister just called again.
reply: That sounds really frustrating, and I'm glad you told me. I love you both, so I'm not going to take sides or pass things along to our brother. I think this needs saying to him directly. Want me to set up a call with the three of us on Sunday? I'll tell him exactly the same thing.
note: Offer to host the conversation, never to carry the message.

situation: My friend Leah is mad at me because I won't take her side against Chloe after their falling out over the bridesmaid thing. She says I'm being fake.
reply: I get that you wanted me in your corner, and I'm sorry that's hard. I'm not taking sides between you and Chloe, and that's not me being fake, it's me caring about you both. I'm still your friend, and that hasn't changed.
note: Repeat the position calmly and reaffirm the friendship; don't relitigate their fight to prove you're neutral.

situation: Team lead here. Two of my engineers, Omar and Beth, have been sniping at each other in code reviews. I've spoken to each privately; now I'm hosting a joint meeting tomorrow. How do I open it?
reply: Thanks for coming, both of you. I'm not here to decide who was right in past reviews. Let's keep this to how code reviews work from here on: one person talks at a time, and we leave with one thing we both agree to try for the next two weeks. Omar, do you want to start with what a good review looks like to you?
note: Neutral on the history, clear on the rules. Send a written summary of the agreement afterwards.

situation: 我跟阿杰、小雨三个人合租。他们俩因为打扫轮值和水电费闹翻了，一周没说话，两个人都跑来跟我吐槽。刚才小雨让我帮她跟阿杰说一声，下个月网费她不跟他平摊了。
reply: 小雨，我知道这事让你挺憋屈的，你愿意跟我说我很理解。不过我不想在你们俩中间传话，传着传着意思就变了，对谁都不好。网费的事还是你直接跟阿杰说比较好。要不这周日晚上八点我们三个在客厅坐下来聊一次？只聊网费和打扫，一个人说完另一个再说，争取先定下一件事。我也会这样跟阿杰说，不是突然袭击。
note: 拒绝当传话筒，但主动搭一个直接对话的台子；两边说一样的话，才是真的中立。

situation: My mom and my aunt haven't spoken since Grandma's funeral in June, over who gets her house. I offered to host a call between them and my aunt texted: 'Never. And if you keep pushing this I'll stop talking to you too.'
reply: I hear you, and I'm not going to push. I love you both and I'm staying out of the house question. The offer stands if you ever want it, and either way, nothing changes between you and me.
note: When one side refuses, drop it cleanly and protect your own relationship with her; the offer stays open without pressure.

situation: I chair our community garden committee. I got two members, Frank and Delia, together to sort out their fight over the shared tool shed, and 10 minutes in they're talking over each other and Frank just said 'this is pointless'. I need to stop it.
reply: Let's stop here for today. I don't think we'll get further right now, and that's okay; it's obvious you both care about this garden. I'd like to try again on Saturday the 10th, just on the shed schedule. If it helps, I can look into whether there's a community mediation service nearby that could send someone to sit in.
note: Pause kindly, name the shared goal, and offer a narrower second try or a neutral professional. Don't rule on the shed in the room.

situation: I manage a small sales team. Priya and Luke have been fighting over who owns the Harmon Foods account since the territory change. In our joint meeting today we agreed Priya owns it from Oct 1, Luke hands over his notes and contacts by Oct 2 and joins the next two calls, and disputes come to me instead of the team chat. I want it in writing to both.
reply: Thanks both for today. To confirm what we agreed: Priya owns the Harmon Foods account from Thursday 1 October. Luke will share his account notes and contacts by Friday 2 October and join the next two Harmon calls to make the introductions. If anything about the account is unclear from here, bring it to me rather than the team channel. Let's check in together on Tuesday 13 October.
note: The written summary goes to both at once, in the same words: neutral on who was right, clear on who does what next.

situation: 我不是领导，只是组里的普通同事。小王和小李为了一个项目排期闹得很僵，两个人都私下跟我抱怨对方。今天小王又来找我，说：“你评评理，是不是他太过分了？”
reply: 我知道这事让你挺窝火的，你愿意跟我说我明白。不过我跟你俩都是同事，谁对谁错我真不好评，评了反而帮倒忙，你跟我说的我也不会传给小李。排期的事还是你俩直接聊最快，要不约个会议室把时间线摊开对一对？需要的话，我可以帮你想想怎么开口。
note: 同级同事被拉去评理：先接住情绪，说明不站队、不传话，再把他推向直接沟通；领导的角色留给领导。

situation: 大学四个室友的群里，阿敏和小月因为国庆去厦门的AA账吵起来了，越说越难听，其他人都不敢出声。钱是我统一垫付的，民宿和包车的单据都在我这儿。我想在群里说点什么。
reply: 两位，看得出这事让你们俩都挺不舒服的，我不站谁那边。钱是我垫的，今晚我把民宿和包车的每一笔单据整理成表格发到群里，大家按实际花费看。对得上的就按表来，有出入的地方你们俩私下直接聊，需要的话周六晚上我们三个语音一下，我在旁边。群里这事就先聊到这儿。
note: 群里公开吵，先把争执挪出群聊；垫钱的人只提供事实，不判谁对谁错，再搭一个直接对话的台子。

situation: My two closest friends, Jess and Mia, haven't spoken since a fight over a flat they were meant to share. My 30th is Saturday Oct 17 at my place and I want both there. I'd like to tell each of them before they see the other on the invite.
reply: Heads up so there are no surprises: I've invited Mia to my 30th on Saturday the 17th as well. I'm not trying to set anything up, and I'm telling her the same about you. I'd really love you there. If it feels like too much, I get it, and we'll do dinner just us the week after.
note: Same words to both, sent separately: no ambush, no engineered reunion, and a real out that protects your friendship with each.

situation: Nina and Jordan from my climbing group split up last month. Nina told me Jordan has turned up outside her flat three nights running and texted her that she'll 'regret this'. Jordan has now asked me to get the two of them together to 'talk it out', and I want to message Nina.
reply: Nina, thank you for telling me, and I'm so sorry you're dealing with this. Turning up at your flat and that text aren't a falling-out for me to help smooth over, so I won't be setting up any meeting between you. Please report both to the police, keep the text, and if he turns up again and you feel unsafe, call the emergency number straight away. If you'd like someone with you when you report it, I'm free tomorrow evening.
note: Threats and turning up uninvited are not a two-sided dispute: don't mediate or arrange a meeting, point her to the police, and don't pass anything she told you back to him.

situation: I'm a shift supervisor at a restaurant. A server, Jade, told me a line cook, Ryan, keeps commenting on her body and has brushed against her twice. She asked me to 'just sit you both down and sort it out' because she doesn't want it to be a big deal.
reply: Jade, thank you for telling me, and I'm really sorry this has been happening. What you've described isn't a disagreement I can sort out between the two of you; it has to go to HR, and that's what protects you. I'm taking it to HR today, and I'll keep it as private as I can. I'll also ask them to keep you and Ryan on separate shifts while it's looked into. Is there anything else you need from me right now?
note: Comments about her body and unwanted touching are harassment, not a two-sided dispute: no joint sit-down, report it to HR, and don't promise outcomes HR decides.

situation: 我妈从老家过来帮我们带刚满半岁的孩子，跟我老婆因为孩子穿多少、什么时候加辅食天天闹别扭，两个人都私下跟我抱怨对方。刚才我妈又拉着我说：“你得管管你媳妇，她根本不听我的。”
reply: 妈，我知道您大老远过来帮我们带孩子，受了委屈，您跟我说我都明白。不过我不想在您和她之间传话，传来传去意思就变了。孩子穿多少、什么时候加辅食，这周六孩子睡午觉的时候，咱们三个坐下来一起商量个规矩，一件一件说，一个人说完另一个再说，拿不准的就一起听儿保医生的。我也会跟她说一样的话，不偏向谁。
note: 婆媳之间，你是孩子的爸爸，可以有自己的意见，但不当传话筒，把两个人拉到一张桌上一起定规矩。

situation: Three weeks ago I sat down with my neighbours Hal and Rosa, who'd been fighting for months over our shared driveway, and they agreed a parking schedule. It seems to be holding. I want to check in once with each of them without stirring it all up again.
reply: Hi Hal, just checking in now it's been a few weeks since we sat down about the driveway. From the outside the schedule seems to be working, and I'm really glad. If anything needs tweaking, a quick word with Rosa directly is probably the best route, and I'm happy to put the kettle on for both of you again if you'd like that. Otherwise I'll leave you to it.
note: One check-in, the same words to each of them, then genuinely step back; don't audit how the deal is going.

situation: At dinner on Saturday my best friend Sophie joked that my husband Tom 'finally found a job that sticks', and he's been fuming since. Sophie just texted asking if Tom is mad at her and whether I can smooth it over for her.
reply: Hey Soph, thanks for asking, and I'd rather Tom tell you how he took it than me guessing on his behalf. I love you both, so I'm staying out of the middle on this one. If you want to clear the air, a quick text to him directly will mean more than anything passed through me, and I'm happy to help you word it.
note: When one side is your partner, neutrality matters more: don't report his feelings, point her to him, and keep your friendship with her separate.

situation: 我和未婚夫阿哲下个月结婚。我爸妈离婚十年了，关系很僵，为了主桌怎么坐、我爸要不要带现在的妻子来，两个人都分别打电话给我，让我去跟对方说。刚才我妈又让我告诉我爸：“他要带那个人来，我就不去了。”
reply: 妈，我知道这事让您心里很不好受，您愿意跟我说，我都明白。不过我不想在您和爸之间传话，传来传去只会更僵。婚礼那天我最想要的，就是您和爸都在。座位和来宾怎么安排，我和阿哲商量好自己定，定好了分别告诉您和爸，跟他说的也会是一样的话。您有什么担心的随时跟我说，我们一起想办法让您那天待得舒服些。
note: 争的是你自己的婚礼时，不替任何一方传话，也不裁判谁对谁错，安排由你和伴侣来定，再用同样的话分别告诉两边。

situation: I'm one of three co-founders of a 9-person startup. Ana (CTO) and Ben (CEO) have been clashing for two weeks over whether to launch in November or January. Ben just DMed me: 'You were in Monday's meeting, just tell Ana she agreed to November.'
reply: Ben, I can hear how frustrated you are, and I get why the date matters so much to you. I'm not going to referee who said what on Monday or carry it to Ana; a ruling from me won't settle it between you two. What we all want is a launch that holds up. Can the three of us sit down on Friday, each of you lays out your case without interruption, and we leave with a date and what has to be true to hit it? I'll say the same to Ana.
note: Being asked to act as a witness is still being asked to pick a side; move it to a joint conversation with ground rules.

situation: 我是二年级班主任。课间乐乐和浩浩推搡，乐乐摔倒磕破了膝盖，校医已经处理过。晚上两家家长在班级群里吵起来，互相指责，乐乐妈妈和浩浩爸爸又分别私信我，让我主持公道。
reply: 乐乐妈妈您好，乐乐膝盖磕破了，您心疼着急，我完全理解，校医已经处理过，这几天我也会多留意他。这件事我不在群里评判谁对谁错，群里说下去只会越来越僵，也请您先别在群里继续了。想请您和浩浩爸爸10月8日周四下午4点半来学校，我们三个坐下来，把当时的情况和两个孩子各自说的都摊开，一个人说完另一个再说，争取商量出一个两家都能接受的办法。浩浩爸爸那边我也是这么说的。您看这个时间可以吗？
note: 老师夹在两家家长中间：先把争吵移出群聊，两边收到同样的话，再约一次有规则的当面沟通，不在私信里替任何一方下结论。

situation: I moderate a 2,000-member Discord server for a board game. Two long-time members, Kai and Rowan, have been sniping at each other in #general for a week over a tournament ruling. Kai just DMed me asking me to ban Rowan and 'back him up in public'.
reply: Hey Kai, thanks for coming to me rather than going another round in #general, and I can tell this ruling really got to you. I'm not going to take a side between you and Rowan, and I'm not banning anyone over a disagreement. What I am asking is that you both take it out of #general from now on, and I'm telling Rowan exactly the same. If you'd like to talk it through with him directly, I'm happy to set up a DM with the three of us this weekend.
note: Neutral on the dispute, not on channel behaviour; if it turns into harassment it is a moderation matter, not a mediation.

situation: My best friends Carol and Bea fell out over what Bea's hen do was going to cost. Last week Bea vented to me, including that she thinks Carol is 'tight with money'. Now Carol has messaged me: 'Be honest, what has Bea been saying about me?'
reply: Carol, I can tell this is really eating at you, and I get why you'd want to know. I'm not going to pass on what either of you says to me, the same way I wouldn't tell Bea what you've told me. If you want to know where she stands, she's the one to ask, and I'm happy to help you think about how to start that conversation.
note: Keep confidences: no hints either way, not even 'she wasn't that harsh', and the same rule applies to both.

situation: I own a small bakery with four staff. After weeks of friction over who cleans the ovens at close, my head baker Rita texted me tonight: 'Either Kev goes or I do.' Kev is our newest baker. I don't want to lose either of them.
reply: Rita, thank you for telling me straight, and I can hear how fed up you are. I'm not going to settle this with an ultimatum, and I'm not ruling on who's in the right about the ovens. What I will do is fix the closing routine: I'd like the three of us to sit down on Friday after close, agree who cleans what and when, and I'll put it up on the wall. Before then, is there anything you want me to know?
note: Neutral on who's right, firm on the fix; if Rita describes harassment rather than friction, it's no longer a mediation.

situation: 我老伴上周中风住院了。女儿这周请了三天假在医院陪护，儿子说工作忙只来过一次，两个人为了陪护怎么排、护工钱怎么分吵翻了，都跑来跟我说对方的不是。刚才女儿打电话，让我去跟她哥说“别总拿工作忙当借口”。
reply: 闺女，这几天你请假在医院守着你爸，妈都看在眼里，知道你累，也知道你委屈。不过你和你哥之间的话，妈不传，传来传去只会更僵。周六下午你们俩都来医院，咱们三个在病房外面坐下来，就商量陪护怎么排、护工钱怎么分这两件事，一个人说完另一个再说。我也会这样跟你哥说。你爸这时候最需要的，是咱们一家人齐心。
note: A parent between two adult children: acknowledge the one who is carrying more, still refuse to carry the message.

situation: My mum, Rosa, speaks only Spanish and my husband, Mark, speaks only English, so I translate whenever they talk. They've been clashing over whether our son's christening is at Mum's church in Seville or here in Leeds, and Mark just texted me: 'Tell your mum she's being controlling.' We're all on a video call with her on Sunday anyway.
reply: I get why you're frustrated. I'm not going to pass that line on to Mum, though: anything that goes through me comes out sharper, in either language. On Sunday's call I'll translate whatever you both say, word for word, so you can tell her yourself how you feel about the venue. Want to think through how to put it before then?
note: When you're the interpreter, offer to translate a direct conversation faithfully rather than deliver one-sided messages.

situation: My two teenagers, Maya (16) and Leo (14), have been fighting for weeks over the family laptop, which they both need for homework; last night it ended in shouting and a slammed door. Each has come to me separately saying the other hogs it. I want to talk to Maya first, then get the three of us to sit down on Sunday afternoon and agree a schedule.
reply: Maya, I can see how fed up you are with the laptop situation, and I'm glad you came to me. I'm not going to rule on who's been worse, and I won't pass on what you've told me to Leo. What I'd like is the three of us at the kitchen table on Sunday afternoon: just the laptop schedule, each of you says what you need without being interrupted, and we leave with a plan stuck on the fridge. I'm saying exactly the same to Leo.
note: A parent could just impose a rota, but one they agree to together sticks better; stay neutral on who's worse, and clear that shouting isn't how it gets settled.

situation: 我是做代账的会计，给一家咖啡馆记账三年。咖啡馆是阿峰和小芸合伙开的，有合伙协议，但利润分配写得很笼统，最近两人为今年的利润怎么分吵翻了，都单独打电话给我。刚才阿峰让我去跟小芸说按他的方案分才合理，还问小芸私下跟我说了什么。
reply: 阿峰，我理解这事让你挺上火的。不过我是给你们俩共同记账的，利润怎么分不该由我来定，我不会替任何一方去说服另一方，你们各自跟我说的话我也不会转述。我能做的是把今年的收支和你们各自的投入整理成一份清楚的数字，10月7日周三前同时发给你们俩。怎么分最好以合伙协议为准，协议没写清楚的部分，你们俩坐下来谈；需要的话我可以在场只讲数字，也可以请律师或调解员帮忙。
note: 专业角色更要中立：同一份数字同时给双方，分钱的规则交给协议和他们自己。

situation: I rent out a four-bedroom house by the room. One tenant, Priya, emailed that her housemate Sam games with his headset mic on until about 2am most nights, she hears him through the wall, and she asked me to 'have a word'. Every tenancy agreement includes a house rule of quiet hours from 11pm to 7am.
reply: Hi Priya, thanks for telling me, and I'm sorry it's been keeping you up. I won't pass on what you've said or take sides between you and Sam, but quiet hours from 11pm to 7am are in everyone's tenancy agreement, so I'll send a reminder about them to the whole house today. If it carries on, a direct chat between you two is usually the quickest fix, and I'm happy to sit in on one if you'd both like that.
note: As the landlord you're neutral on the personal dispute but not on the house rules: remind everyone, keep her complaint private, and offer to host a direct talk.

situation: Meine Freunde Jonas und Lukas reden seit zwei Wochen nicht mehr miteinander, seit Jonas beim Junggesellenabschied einen blöden Witz über Lukas' Freundin gemacht hat. Jetzt schreibt Jonas mir: „Kannst du Lukas sagen, dass es mir leid tut?“ Ich mag beide und will nicht der Bote sein.
reply: Schön, dass du dich entschuldigen willst, Jonas, das ist ein guter Schritt. Ich gebe es aber nicht weiter: Eine Entschuldigung kommt viel besser an, wenn sie direkt von dir kommt und nicht über mich. Schreib ihm selbst oder ruf ihn an. Wenn du magst, überlegen wir zusammen, wie du es formulierst.
note: Auch eine gute Nachricht nicht weitertragen: Über Dritte wirkt eine Entschuldigung halbherzig, direkt wirkt sie.

situation: 我孙子小宇读大三，想休学一年去打电竞，他爸（我儿子建军）坚决不同意，父子俩吵得一周没说话，都跑来跟我诉苦。刚才小宇打电话让我去劝劝他爸，说“爸只听你的”。这周日10月4日中午他们俩本来就要来我这儿吃饭。
reply: 小宇，你愿意跟奶奶说心里话，奶奶很高兴，也知道你这几天心里不好受。不过这事奶奶不替你去劝你爸，也不替你爸来劝你，你跟我说的话我不会转给他。休学是大事，还得你们父子俩当面说。这周日中午你们本来就要来吃饭，吃完饭咱们三个坐下来，就聊这一件事：你先把打算从头讲一遍，你爸听完再说他的担心，谁都别插嘴。我也会这样跟你爸说。
note: 长辈被一方请去当说客：接住情绪，但不当说客、不传话，把两个人拉到同一张桌上，规则提前讲好。

situation: Two friends from my running club, Dan and Ella, fell out after Dan pulled out of their relay team two days before the race. When Dan vented to me last week I said Ella was overreacting; he repeated it to her, and she's just messaged me: 'So you think I'm overreacting?' I want to own that and get back to being neutral.
reply: You're right, I did say that to Dan, and I shouldn't have. I'd only heard his side, and it wasn't fair to you. I'm sorry. From here on I'm not taking sides between you two, and I won't pass anything on either way. If you and Dan want to talk it through directly, I'm happy to help set that up; if not, that's completely fine, and nothing changes between us.
note: If you've already taken a side, own it in one line and reset; don't defend the comment or repeat anything else Dan said.

situation: 我爸妈都六十多了，为了要不要卖掉老家的房子、搬到杭州离我近点，吵了一个月：我爸想搬，我妈舍不得老邻居。两人轮流给我打电话，刚才我爸说：“你劝劝你妈，她最听你的。”10月3日我回家过节。
reply: 爸，我知道您想搬过来，是想离我们近一点，这份心我明白。不过这事我不去劝妈，也不替妈来劝您，你们俩跟我说的话我都不往对面传。房子是你们俩的，得你们俩商量着定。10月3日我回家，到时候咱们三个坐下来，就聊这一件事：您先说想搬的理由，妈再说她舍不得什么，一个人说完另一个再说，不急着当天就定。我也会跟妈说一样的话。
note: 父母之间的事，子女即使有自己的偏好也不当说客：两边同样的话，搭一个有规则的当面谈。
